result.title: Executable Archaeology: Reanimating the Logic Theorist
result.comment: This paper builds upon a previous ArXiv paper of a similar name: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.13514. This paper is NOT a mere rehash of the previous paper; appropriate citations and comparison are provided in the discussion. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible
result.summary: The Logic Theorist (LT), created by Allen Newell, J. C. Shaw, and Herbert Simon in 1955--1956, is regarded by some as the first artificial intelligence program. It was originally simulated by hand and written in a pseudocode called the Logic Language (LL), which was later called Information Processing Language One (IPL-I). LT was revised many times. The first machine-executed version was written in IPL-II and ran on the JOHNNIAC, and a late version was published in 1963 by Einar Stefferud as a pedagogical document and written in IPL-V, the only version of IPL that was formally released to the public. We describe a reanimation of both the IPL-I (LL) version of LT and the 1963 IPL-V version. Comparing the two reanimations illuminates the process of the invention of early AI algorithms and computer languages.
